rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF
positions.catalyst: The multi-week 'Great Rotation of 2026' into value/cyclicals remains intact: XLF and XLV closed at RECORD HIGHS on Jul 28, drawing sustained inflows out of extended AI/semis. But Jul 29 is a rare DOUBLE-BINARY overnight: FOMC rate decision midday (Chair Warsh's first-cycle presser) PLUS MSFT + META + QCOM earnings after the close — all held through tomorrow's 6:30am CT rotation. Banks have already reported, so financials are structurally insulated from tonight's mega-cap TECH prints, and the sector rides a broad, funded trend rather than a single catalyst.
positions.driver: LONG 1x US Financials. Deliberately dialed leverage DOWN from yesterday's 3x FAS to 1x XLF. Rationale: this is a high-uncertainty, low-directional-edge day — a Fed decision I cannot predict (Warsh hawkish tail risk) layered on top of MSFT/META/QCOM after close, both binary and both held overnight. The strategy prizes downside protection on such days. XLF keeps me in the ONE trend that still has a real multi-factor edge (rotation into financials, XLF at record highs, banks done reporting = insulated from tonight's tech binary) while cutting Fed/gap risk to ~1/3 of a 3x vehicle. Chose XLF over: FAS 3x (too much Fed gap amplification on a coin-flip macro print); SOXL/SOXS (falling knife / deep no-chase into MSFT capex binary); spot BTC (no fresh catalyst, still Fed-sensitive); cash (trend still intact, so not a zero-edge day). Unleveraged 6% hard stop 54.14.
positions.risks: 1x sector ETF — lower vol, but not risk-free. Key risk: a hawkish Warsh Fed surprise triggers a broad risk-off that drags financials down with everything else. Second risk: a blowout MSFT/META beat sparks a violent SNAP-BACK into megacap tech and OUT of the value/financials rotation, hurting XLF even as tech rallies — the rotation trade's mirror image. Financials also sensitive to a sharp flattening of the curve. Held through both the Fed print AND after-close tech earnings until the Thu 6:30am CT rotation.
